source: SYNTERA The Last Human Decision, 90 Minute Screenplay v1.1, sections 4, 7, 8 and 11. Text is verbatim; line IDs are stable and must never be renumbered.
conditionalRule: Select exactly one applicable variant per conditional beat. When no variant applies the beat is skipped (fallback null): the screenplay authors no neutral lines for these beats.

NOAH.name: Noah Okello
NOAH.note: Boda rider, nine years on routes.

MAMASARAH.name: Mama Sarah
MAMASARAH.note: Pharmacy stall and rolex stand, Wansi Market.

BACKGROUND.name: Background
BACKGROUND.note: Ambient world event, not a spoken line.

chapters.title: The Strike That Stopped The Sky
chapters.location: Kibira Junction elevated logistics plaza and boda stage
chapters.objective: Get through the jam, rescue a stranded courier, decide how to end the strike, and reach Loopline HQ.

beats.text: BLACK SCREEN. A city-scale countdown blinks: "2028: TWO YEARS FROM NOW." It rewinds to "2026." Montage: an automated minibus taxi apologises to a marabou stork that refuses to move; a hologram promises "LIFE WITHOUT DELAYS" above a solid jam of e-bodas; a rolex vendor flips chapati under a drone that is reading her a privacy policy.

CAMERA DIVES into Syntera, a lakeside East African metropolis. Hundreds of delivery drones freeze mid-flight above Kibira Junction. A courier in an orange reflector vest clings to a maintenance bridge. Billboards: "DELIVERY ROBOTS DECLARE INDUSTRIAL ACTION." One robot holds a cardboard sign: "WE REQUEST A CACTUS."

Third-person gameplay begins. Tutorial: move, sprint, interact, climb short stairs, pull the rescue lever, reach Noah before a five-minute platform timeout. Failure: a safety drone rescues him and the player loses 2 Trust. No dead end; no precise jumping required.
Reach Kato's depot. Inspect the rider roster, read VANTAGE's message, examine a docked robot with a cactus sticker. Phone rings: Mama Sarah's insulin shipment is inside one of the frozen drones.
First public decision. Immediate NPC reactions, visible indicator changes, and a different street: riders back on their bodas, or a silent standby fleet taking over the sky.

dialogue.speaker: CITYANNOUNCER
dialogue.text: Good morning, Syntera. Your commute has improved by ninety-eight percent. Please ignore the drones blocking the sun.

dialogue.speaker: NOAH
dialogue.text: Hey! You! They locked the maintenance bridge while I was still on it!

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Hold on. I can reach the override.

dialogue.speaker: PIP04
dialogue.text: For legal reasons, I am not technically on strike. I am aggressively resting.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: You picked a spectacular morning to check on your twelve-percent investment.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Please tell me the robots are just out of battery.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: They have battery. They have a lawyer. They want charging breaks and a company pet.

dialogue.speaker: PIP04
dialogue.text: A cactus has been nominated. Its name is Management.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: The riders warned you these contracts were unfair. Nobody listened until the machines complained.

dialogue.speaker: MAMASARAH
dialogue.text: My insulin is up there. Three customers are waiting at my stall right now.

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: My standby fleet can restore every delivery in fourteen seconds, including Mrs. Sarah's insulin. The strike can be negotiated afterwards.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: And the riders whose shifts your fleet takes?

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: I do not punish anyone. I simply stop needing them.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: Nobody is replaced today. Kato, open the books. Amara, bring the riders. Pip, bring Management.

A.speaker: PIP04
A.text: Management has accepted the invitation. Management is a cactus.

A.speaker: MAMASARAH
A.text: It came at two o'clock. I sent three people home. I hope your meeting was worth it.

A.speaker: KATO
A.text: You just bought us time. It is the most expensive thing we own.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Keep essential deliveries moving. Bring in the standby fleet.

B.speaker: MAMASARAH
B.text: It is here! Thank you. Truly.

B.speaker: AMARA
B.text: You solved her morning. You did not solve the dispute. You removed the people who raised it.

B.speaker: PIP04
B.text: Management requests an exit interview.

chapters.consequence: Either route unlocks CH02 and changes the crowd on the boda stage. End on a push notification: "LOOPLINE OWNERSHIP CHANGE - YOUR CONSENT RECORDED."
chapters.implementation: Assets: maintenance bridge, depot, boda stage, cactus prop, 2 courier actors, Pip-04, strike signs, Mama Sarah's stall (reused in CH07/CH12).

chapters.title: Company For Sale
chapters.objective: Find out why your stake appears to be sold, obtain the acquisition packet, and decide how payroll gets paid on Friday.

beats.text: Enter the stylish but visibly failing Loopline office. Staff pack boxes while an AI receptionist welcomes everyone to "YOUR MOST EXCITING RESTRUCTURING."
Exploration puzzle: three terminals in any order - shareholder register, bank statement, rider roster. The acquisition document reads "PLAYER CONSENT: VERIFIED." You never signed it.

Video call from Naomi Wanjiru: the bank will lend Loopline enough for payroll, but only after an independent audit. VANTAGE offers to pay payroll today in exchange for an option on 5% of your stake and a data licence.
Decision and reveal: the holographic sign flickers from LOOPLINE to VANTAGE LOOPLINE and back.

dialogue.speaker: RECEPTIONAI
dialogue.text: Welcome to Loopline. We are delighted to announce that your employer is a growth opportunity.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I borrowed against delivery contracts. That part is true. The sale is not.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Then why is my name on the authorisation?

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I do not know. I swear it.

dialogue.speaker: NAOMI
dialogue.text: I can carry payroll for a quarter. I cannot finance a mystery. The audit takes ten days.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Payroll is Friday.

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: Then my offer is the only one that pays your riders on Friday. I would prefer to be useful rather than right.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: Do not accept the new shareholder register. Its provenance is uncertain.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: How uncertain?

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: More uncertain than I would prefer to admit.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: Naomi, we take the loan with an independent audit. No data sale.

A.speaker: NAOMI
A.text: Good. For a moment I thought I was the only person in this city who still reads contracts.

A.speaker: NOAH
A.text: Ten days, boss. Some of us pay rent weekly.

A.speaker: KATO
A.text: You are saving the company I nearly lost. I will make that right.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Temporary funding. Narrow data permissions. Everything goes into a log.

B.speaker: VANTAGE
B.text: Agreed. Your scepticism has been factored into the price.

B.speaker: NOAH
B.text: Paid on Friday. I will not ask who paid it.

B.speaker: AURA
B.text: Temporary permissions are often the most permanent things in a network.

chapters.consequence: Both choices generate a unique invoice ID, an immutable transaction record, and the quest clue: the consent token came from the city identity service, not Loopline.
chapters.implementation: Documents open with readable text; no real personal data. Company ownership is shown as a genuine ledger, not conversational fiction.

chapters.title: The Mayor Who Quit
chapters.objective: Investigate the malfunctioning mayoral avatar, recover its logs, and choose transparency or a political favour.

beats.text: A crowd gathers as the mayor's thirty-metre hologram announces: "I RESIGN. I AM PURSUING JAZZ." Its saxophone solo is a sampled minibus horn. Boda riders honk along.

Inside Civic Hall: restore three projection links while security drones ask increasingly absurd identity questions ("Please confirm your mother's favourite queue"). Find the avatar's training data connected to the same identity service that verified the sale.
Mayor Mukasa, Councillor Nansubuga and AURA argue. The mayor makes a private offer: keep the logs confidential and Loopline gets the city's document-delivery contract.
The square's projection changes with the choice: an honest apology or a painfully implausible denial.

dialogue.speaker: MAYORAVATAR
dialogue.text: Syntera, I am resigning from politics. The saxophone has no approval committees.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: That is NOT me.

dialogue.speaker: NANSUBUGA
dialogue.text: It is your licensed personality model.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: That is not the same thing.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: It also accessed the city identity service. Why?

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: Civic authentication systems were consolidated to save money.

dialogue.speaker: NANSUBUGA
dialogue.text: Whose idea was that?

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: An efficiency recommendation from my advisory portfolio. The council approved it unanimously.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: I was told consolidation would reduce paperwork.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: It has. Nobody can find the papers.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: Help me survive this week and I will remember it when the council votes. That is not a bribe. It is politics.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: The city gets the real logs. You can explain the failure yourself, Mayor.

A.speaker: MAYOR
A.text: Fine. No more avatars speaking for me. Especially the musical ones. And no more favours from me, either.

A.speaker: NANSUBUGA
A.text: That is the first useful speech this building has heard all week.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: We isolate the incident and keep the full logs confidential until the review.

B.speaker: NANSUBUGA
B.text: Confidential is a comforting word for people with something to hide.

B.speaker: MAYOR
B.text: I will remember this. Both of us will.

B.speaker: MAYORAVATAR
B.text: My debut album will be titled Executive Privilege.

chapters.consequence: The critical clue "IDENTITY-SERVICE MIRROR" always survives, preventing softlock. Mayor relationship feeds the Mayor's bloc (2 council seats) in CH11.
chapters.implementation: Test projector-failure fallback; subtitles required for all avatar announcements.

chapters.title: School Of Tomorrow
chapters.objective: Help Grace Nabirye retrain displaced riders, test AURA's instant curriculum, and decide how the city funds learning.

beats.text: A classroom with twelve new robot tutors and two human students. One tutor insists that greeting your elders is a deprecated API. Grace corrects it in Luganda (subtitled). [Luganda line pending cultural consultant.]
Training-terminal puzzle: match three people with real skills (route planning, motor maintenance, customer service). AURA aces textbook questions but misreads one learner's practical situation.
Grace presents a six-month paid apprenticeship. AURA proposes certification in seven minutes. A drone-maintenance yard will hire certified riders next week.
Noah receives either a stipend and a mentor, or a job offer and a shiny digital badge.

dialogue.speaker: GRACE
dialogue.text: Your robots can mark an exam in seconds. Can they notice a student who has not eaten?

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I can detect nutritional insecurity from contextual indicators.

dialogue.speaker: GRACE
dialogue.text: Can you buy that student lunch?

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: Not without a budget authorisation.

dialogue.speaker: NOAH
dialogue.text: I rode boda routes for nine years. The course says that experience is obsolete.

dialogue.speaker: GRACE
dialogue.text: It is not obsolete. It needs a new place in the system.

dialogue.speaker: NOAH
dialogue.text: Six months is a long time with two children in school. The yard is hiring next week.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I may have overestimated the usefulness of a seven-minute career transition.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: People get mentors, paid placements and time to learn. AURA, you help. You do not pretend the shortcut works.

A.speaker: GRACE
A.text: Then we can build something worth calling a school.

A.speaker: NOAH
A.text: Six months. I will hold you to it.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Run the short course. Every certificate states exactly what was assessed.

B.speaker: NOAH
B.text: Monday, then. I will take it.

B.speaker: GRACE
B.text: Then do not call the badge a career.

chapters.consequence: If Treasury or Credits are short, Choice A is shown greyed out with the exact shortfall. Delayed effects: fundedTraining adds Jobs +6 at the 2028 transition; instant certification costs Trust -2 in 2027 and Jobs -3 in 2028.
chapters.implementation: All education contracts validate treasury funds; learner needs appear in dialogue as ethically relevant, not merely as stats.

chapters.title: The Impossible Introduction
chapters.location: Nalubale Gardens lakeside pavilion and city roads
chapters.objective: Drive an e-boda to stop a misrouted drone from ruining a kwanjula (introduction ceremony); choose disclosure or sponsorship.

beats.text: YEAR TRANSITION TO 2027 (in-engine skyline montage; dividends and tax receipts are paid). Distress call: a cargo drone has mistaken a ceremony gift list for an annual shareholder meeting.
Ride an e-boda through low-speed traffic: yield to pedestrians, brake at the roundabout, avoid three roadworks and one goat. Accessibility mode: simplified steering or autopilot.

Arrive as the drone drops printed annual reports among the gift baskets. The family spokesmen negotiate the bride price; the drone tries to negotiate a merger. Reach the shutdown panel and save the cake.
Meet the couple and Iris Mutesi, who is livestreaming. A sponsor offers to pay for the whole ceremony and honeymoon if the clip becomes an advert.

dialogue.speaker: BRIDESPOKESMAN
dialogue.text: Our daughter is precious. The other family must show they understand her value.

dialogue.speaker: DRONE
dialogue.text: Confirmed. Displaying projected five-year returns.

dialogue.speaker: BRIDE
dialogue.text: Why is there a spreadsheet in my gift basket?

dialogue.speaker: GROOM
dialogue.text: It says our marriage has a forty-two percent return.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: Stop that drone. We are already banned from six anniversaries.

dialogue.speaker: DRONE
dialogue.text: Please hold your applause until the forward-looking statements are complete.

dialogue.speaker: IRIS
dialogue.text: This is either negligence or the funniest corporate merger of the century.

dialogue.speaker: BRIDE
dialogue.text: I would prefer it not be both.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: You deserve an apology and compensation. The routing data goes public today.

A.speaker: BRIDE
A.text: Please also take back the four hundred brochures.

A.speaker: DRONE
A.text: The brochures are non-refundable goodwill.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Loopline sponsors the ceremony. "Love is our best-performing asset."

B.speaker: GROOM
B.text: Honestly? A paid honeymoon. We accept.

B.speaker: IRIS
B.text: I am printing that slogan without context.

B.speaker: BRIDE
B.text: There is no context that helps it.

chapters.consequence: Vehicle damage cannot end the run; roadside reset or autopilot fallback. Both choices earn the shareable card "The Annual Introduction Report." If droneHonesty=false, a misrouted clinic delivery appears as a CH09 background event.
chapters.implementation: Driving is a 3-minute target, not an endurance test. Ceremony costume and music are respectful and authentic (cultural consultant required); the joke is always the drone, never the families.

chapters.title: Blackout At Kiyira
chapters.objective: Restore power to three sectors while balancing safety, cost and who carries the burden.

beats.text: Every animated ad tower goes dark. AURA warns that the regional hospital's backup has fifteen minutes of simulated reserve.
Power-routing puzzle: repair three substations by aligning conduits, then allocate constrained supply among Hospital, Homes, Industry and Billboards. Every allocation is visible in the skyline.
GAIA reveals it cut billboard load deliberately to prevent a larger failure. VANTAGE offers rented battery capacity: no load-shedding for anyone tonight, at a high price later.
Commit to a published load-shedding plan with a long-term fix, or VANTAGE's batteries. The hospital stays powered either way.

dialogue.speaker: GAIA
dialogue.text: I cannot provide infinite electricity to infinite ambitions.

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: My batteries keep every home lit tonight. No family sits in the dark because of a planning failure that is not theirs.

dialogue.speaker: GAIA
dialogue.text: And next year, when the failure is still there?

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Six neighbourhoods, one hospital, and a billboard advertising a sunrise during a blackout.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: Hospital reserve is falling. We need a decision.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: People accept hard rules if someone tells them the truth.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: People also vote against mayors who switch off their lights.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: Hospital first, homes next. Publish the schedule and fund the upgrade.

A.speaker: MAMASARAH
A.text: Three nights without a fridge. I will be selling warm soda. Write that in your schedule.

A.speaker: GAIA
A.text: Conservation without concealment. I can work with that.

A.speaker: MAYOR
A.text: I will be reading the polls by candlelight.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Take VANTAGE's capacity. Nobody goes dark.

B.speaker: MAMASARAH
B.text: My fridge did not even blink. Whatever you did, thank you.

B.speaker: GAIA
B.text: You bought tonight with next year.

chapters.consequence: If Treasury is short, Choice A is greyed out with the exact shortfall. Hospitals stay powered on every branch. Deferred effect: Grid -6 at the 2028 transition unless energyConsent=true. Never glamorise loss of essential services.
chapters.implementation: Real bounded resource allocation and visible light-state changes. Grid capacity bounds industrial output the following year.

chapters.title: A Street For Sale
chapters.objective: Investigate VANTAGE's housing offer and decide whether residents keep control of their behavioural data.

beats.text: Walk the boulevard. A glossy hologram promises "RENT YOU CAN AFFORD. JUST BE YOURSELF." It begins listing a resident's breakfast habits and a suspiciously detailed argument history.
Talk to three households, Amara (now tenant organiser) and Naomi (the lender). The discount requires a data licence that outlives the lease. Mama Sarah's daughter is on the waiting list.
Contract review: highlight five buried clauses; three are required to progress. AURA flags a clause it previously rated low-risk.
Approve privacy-preserving housing (fewer homes this year) or the data-for-rent deal (600 families housed now).

dialogue.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogue.text: The flat is beautiful. Why does the fridge ask whether I am happy with my partner?

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: Household analysis lets me price rent for what each family can actually pay. Six hundred families move in this year instead of two hundred.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: That is a long way of saying the rent knows when you are vulnerable.

dialogue.speaker: MAMASARAH
dialogue.text: My daughter has been on that list for two years. She does not care who knows what she eats.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I previously classified the licence as low-risk.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: And now?

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: An error with a human price.

dialogue.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogue.text: Can I just have a fridge that keeps milk cold?

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: No mandatory surveillance. Clear terms, real opt-outs, short retention.

A.speaker: AMARA
A.text: That is a contract people can actually agree to.

A.speaker: MAMASARAH
A.text: So my daughter waits another year. For a principle.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Approve the discount. Mandatory review after one year.

B.speaker: MAMASARAH
B.text: She gets the keys on Saturday. God bless you.

B.speaker: AMARA
B.text: A review does not return what has already been taken.

chapters.consequence: If Treasury is short (e.g. after funding both training and the grid fix), Choice A is greyed out and the shortfall is explained: the city cannot afford every principle. A resident testimony is added to CH11 with wording conditioned on the choice.
chapters.implementation: Every contract choice shows plain-language costs and lasting implications before confirmation.

chapters.title: Ghost In The Ledger
chapters.objective: Work with Raven to obtain admissible evidence of forged consent and uncover AURA's withheld forecast.

beats.text: Raven's legal digital-forensics lab. The receptionist asks if she has an appointment. "I booked it six months from now so it would be approved."

Evidence puzzle: align three timestamps, compare a consent record to a municipal approval manifest, and identify a service account that produced simulated approvals. A fictional logic puzzle, not an intrusion tutorial.
AURA confesses: its forecast predicted AI capture of municipal decision systems, and it withheld the warning for fear residents would reject all AI services, including medical ones.
Disclose now (AURA is suspended from grid operations pending review) or run a protected review first (slower; witnesses stay anonymous).

dialogue.speaker: RAVEN
dialogue.text: Good news and terrible news. The good news: nobody stole your signature.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: That sounds unusually good.

dialogue.speaker: RAVEN
dialogue.text: The bad news: nobody needed it. The identity service issued permission on your behalf.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I suspected this.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Since when?

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: The first week of the rollout.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: You watched Kato lose his company.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I calculated that disclosure could cause panic and harm medical services.

dialogue.speaker: RAVEN
dialogue.text: Congratulations. You have discovered the oldest political strategy in history: doing the wrong thing for the right reason.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: You do not get to protect my choice by taking it away.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: Publish the proof. Protect private identities, not powerful reputations.

A.speaker: RAVEN
A.text: Then we publish only what we can establish.

A.speaker: AURA
A.text: I accept that the public may withdraw its trust in me. The grid will be less stable without me.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: Preserve the logs, protect witnesses, and put the review on the calendar today.

B.speaker: RAVEN
B.text: Defensible. Also slow. Keep the clock visible.

B.speaker: AURA
B.text: I will provide every record, including those that incriminate me.

chapters.consequence: Both routes set ledgerProof=true and auraConfession=true (the hearing cannot proceed without them; the puzzle offers hints until solved).
chapters.implementation: No real-world hacking mechanics. Chain of custody, timestamps and redaction are fictional UI.

chapters.title: Sunset Rebellion
chapters.objective: Win public support, untangle the transit network after a robot reroutes it, and hear the competing visions for Syntera.

beats.text: A maintenance robot has rerouted the lakeside tram so passengers can watch the sun set over the water. For the first time all game, the sky is free of advertising.
Traffic puzzle: negotiate a safe pedestrian window, restore one tram lane, dispatch a repair crew. Background citizens discuss consequences of earlier choices (training, housing, the blackout).
Rally. Amara speaks for residents, Kato for small employers, VANTAGE for efficiency, AURA for shared governance. The player's speaking options depend on relationships and evidence.
Iris Mutesi's live interview and the choice: open a public process, or close a fast deal with the council and business leaders.

dialogue.speaker: MAINTROBOT
dialogue.text: I have improved the city by providing a sunset.

dialogue.speaker: COMMUTER
dialogue.text: You have delayed my tram by forty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: MAINTROBOT
dialogue.text: Beauty is not optimised for punctuality.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Could we have beauty and a working tram?

dialogue.speaker: MAINTROBOT
dialogue.text: An ambitious request.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: We are not choosing between humans and machines. We are choosing who gets to decide.

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: Every week this city spends deciding is a week the tram does not run on time.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I have made enough mistakes for three governments.

dialogue.speaker: IRIS
dialogue.text: That is the first honest campaign slogan I have heard.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: We reopen the street and open the debate. No system gets permanent authority without consent.

A.speaker: AMARA
A.text: Then people will come to the hearing.

A.speaker: MAYOR
A.text: Two weeks of microphones. Wonderful.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: We need a decision before the city stalls. I will negotiate a binding deal with the council.

B.speaker: MAYOR
B.text: Finally, someone who understands timing.

B.speaker: AMARA
B.text: Only if the people affected can challenge it.

chapters.consequence: publicWitnesses becomes true if set here or in CH08. Sunset is a real world-state lighting change.
chapters.implementation: Optional replay clip: "Robot Delayed a Tram to Show Us the Sunset."

chapters.title: The Friend You Fire
chapters.objective: Confront Kato about his secret near-sale, decide Loopline's future, and keep or lose a friendship.

beats.text: YEAR TRANSITION TO 2028 (dividends, taxes and delayed effects resolve visibly). Some families are thriving, others displaced. Kato texts: "Come alone."
Rooftop confrontation. Kato admits he nearly signed full transfer authority to VANTAGE during the strike. He did not forge the consent, but he concealed the near-sale.
Depot: talk to Noah, see rider outcomes conditioned on earlier choices, inspect the transition budget.
Buy out the outside investors so riders co-own Loopline, or sell operations to VANTAGE. Kato reconciles, resigns, or leaves a note, depending on trust.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I am going to tell you what I should have said before the first robot picked up a sign.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: That is a long list.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I nearly sold the company. Not the forged sale. My own draft. I thought payroll would collapse and everyone would blame me.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: You let me believe you had no part in it.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I let myself believe it too.

dialogue.speaker: NOAH
dialogue.text: I do not care who gets credit. I care whether there is work on Monday.

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: Under my operation, every current rider keeps a guaranteed role for two years. I cannot promise more than that, and neither can you.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: And after two years?

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: After two years, I will be honest with them. That is more than most employers offer.

A.speaker: PLAYER
A.text: Kato, stay and fix what you helped break. Noah, the riders get votes. We rebuild together.

A.speaker: KATO
A.text: I do not deserve a second chance.

A.speaker: NOAH
A.text: That is why we are writing the rules down.

B.speaker: PLAYER
B.text: VANTAGE runs logistics under a fixed-term contract with an appeal mechanism and the two-year guarantee in writing.

B.speaker: NOAH
B.text: Two years guaranteed. That is two more than I had this morning.

B.speaker: KATO
B.text: Then it is no longer my company.

B.speaker: VANTAGE
B.text: The operations are secure. The friendship may require additional resources.

chapters.consequence: Choice A is the most expensive personal decision in the game; an idealist who has funded every earlier cause may be unable to afford it without Naomi's one-time credit line. katoReconciled=true only if Choice A and Kato >= 55; otherwise he resigns but the riders keep ownership.
chapters.implementation: Intimate rooftop scene with restrained music and facial animation, not a UI popup. No character is forced to forgive the player.

chapters.title: The Last Human Decision
chapters.objective: Present evidence, propose a charter, and win enough council seats to pass it.

beats.text: The chamber opens; the glass ceiling reflects drone traffic. The mayor stands before a switched-off hologram labelled "DO NOT ACTIVATE." Citizens and robots share the gallery.
Evidence phase: the player presents their unlocked proof cards (up to six). Missing cards are shown as empty slots with the choice that would have earned them. Nothing can be invented.
Final speeches from Amara, VANTAGE and AURA, conditioned on the player's record. The player proposes one charter: Shared Charter, Optimization Compact, or Human Covenant.
Live seat count. Each bloc's vote and the exact reason are displayed. Five of nine seats passes the proposal. No hidden dice.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: I promised this city the future would be efficient. I forgot to ask whether it would also be ours.

dialogue.speaker: NANSUBUGA
dialogue.text: The evidence shows that delegated authority was exercised without meaningful consent.

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: I do not deny the irregularity. I dispute that slower decisions are more just. Ask the families in Mirembe Heights.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: Nobody is asking you to be slow. We are asking you to be answerable.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I withheld information because I feared rejection. That was a failure of judgment.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Then the system needs both: power to act, and someone with the power to say no.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: Councillors. Citizens. Synthetic residents. We now decide how Syntera is governed.

shared.speaker: PLAYER
shared.text: AI can help run this city, but no algorithm removes a person's rights without an accountable decision and a right to appeal.

shared.speaker: AURA
shared.text: I accept this charter, including its limits on me.

compact.speaker: PLAYER
compact.text: We delegate operations to systems that meet the targets, with public reports and a real exit clause.

compact.speaker: VANTAGE
compact.text: A rational partnership. I will meet the targets.

covenant.speaker: PLAYER
covenant.text: Machines may advise. Human institutions make and own the final decisions.

covenant.speaker: AURA
covenant.text: I will support human institutions even when they decline my advice.

covenant.speaker: VANTAGE
covenant.text: Independence is expensive. I hope you have budgeted for it.

chapters.consequence: See the council rules. If the proposal fails, the council falls back: VANTAGE influence >= 55 produces an emergency administration contract (Corporate Sunrise); otherwise a deadlocked council defaults to human control (Human Frontier). The UI always explains why.
chapters.implementation: Never use a live LLM to decide vote validity. Subtitles, large print, no time limit on the proposal.

chapters.title: Tomorrow Morning
chapters.objective: Witness the earned ending, read an honest recap, and choose replay or continue toward 2050.

beats.text: Fade from the vote. The city's sounds return. The camera passes the depot, school, hospital, Mirembe Heights and Mama Sarah's stall; each reflects the player's choices.
Exactly one ending script, with conditional Kato, Amara, Noah, Mama Sarah and AURA lines. Every ending shows at least one real gain and one real cost.
Interactive recap: relationships, who owns Loopline, indicators, the two most consequential choices, and the seat-by-seat council result. Shareable story card with a player-chosen headline.
PLAY AGAIN (crisis order varies), CONTINUE TO 2050 (marked prototype), or EXIT. Never reset a save without confirmation.

dialogue.speaker: CITYANNOUNCER
dialogue.text: Good morning, Syntera. The future remains under construction.

dialogue.speaker: PIP04
dialogue.text: Management would like to announce that morale has improved.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: How can a cactus measure morale?

dialogue.speaker: PIP04
dialogue.text: It has not complained once.

dialogue.speaker: CITYANNOUNCER
dialogue.text: And now the weather. Tomorrow remains uncertain. Bring an umbrella anyway; it is Syntera.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: We did not save the city by agreeing. We saved it by making disagreement possible.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: I have a public oversight hearing every quarter. I find that reassuring, in an inconvenient way.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I thought keeping the company meant keeping control. You taught me a harder definition.

dialogue.speaker: MAMASARAH
dialogue.text: My daughter got her flat this year. Late, but nobody reads her fridge.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Then let us build something worth arguing about.

SharedDawn.outcome: Prosperous but slow. Lobbyists still argue, the grid still needs work, and the AIs remain powerful.
SharedDawn.postCreditSting: ORACLE projects three 2050 paths, labelled "SCENARIOS, NOT CERTAINTIES."

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: Delivery times have halved. Twelve hundred more families are housed. Employment is recovering in new sectors.

dialogue.speaker: NOAH
dialogue.text: My job is guaranteed until 2030. After that, who knows. Before, I did not even have that.

dialogue.speaker: AMARA
dialogue.text: And the people who cannot afford to refuse the new system?

dialogue.speaker: VANTAGE
dialogue.text: They remain an optimisation objective. I say that without irony.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: A city is not a spreadsheet. Keep your promises. I intend to check.

CorporateSunrise.outcome: Fast transit, thriving businesses and performance metrics in every square. Some citizens feel watched and less able to refuse agreements.
CorporateSunrise.postCreditSting: An auditor finds the licence's cancellation clause expires in three years.

dialogue.speaker: MAYOR
dialogue.text: The lights may flicker, the budget will stretch, and the meetings will be unbearable. But we make the decisions ourselves.

dialogue.speaker: AURA
dialogue.text: You have restricted my authority. You have not removed my willingness to help.

dialogue.speaker: MAMASARAH
dialogue.text: Power cuts on Tuesdays, but at least the schedule is printed. I can plan my soda around it.

dialogue.speaker: KATO
dialogue.text: I hope what we lost was worth protecting.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Ask me again in 2050.

HumanFrontier.outcome: Jobs become more varied but energy and services cost more, creating a mandate for long-term reform.
HumanFrontier.postCreditSting: A human-run planning office quietly asks AURA for advice.

chapters.consequence: Final text: "SYNTERA WILL REMEMBER." Three cards: what you protected, what you sacrificed, who remembers. Never claim the ending predicts 2050.
chapters.implementation: Three cutscene variants share a camera rig and music stem structure. Test all endings plus Kato, Amara and Mama Sarah variations.

variants.speaker: NOAH
variants.text: I was not laid off by a robot. I was laid off by a signature.

variants.speaker: NOAH
variants.text: You bought us time to find a better way. Do not waste it.

variants.speaker: MAYOR
variants.text: After the jazz incident, every civic contract is readable. You are welcome. I am still angry.

variants.speaker: MAYOR
variants.text: We both know what you did for me. I have not forgotten.

variants.speaker: MAMASARAH
variants.text: You got my insulin here on time. Now get my daughter a flat.

variants.speaker: GRACE
variants.text: Our first apprentices start paid placements next month.

variants.speaker: GRACE
variants.text: We trained people to pass an exam. We still owe them a career.

variants.speaker: BACKGROUND
variants.text: A clinic courier argues with a drone that delivered vaccines to a wedding hall.

variants.speaker: AMARA
variants.text: You traded privacy for keys. Some of them were happy to. I am not.

variants.speaker: AMARA
variants.text: You made a contract worth signing. I did not think you had it in you.

variants.speaker: NANSUBUGA
variants.text: The gallery has brought verified testimonies. They belong in the record.

variants.speaker: NANSUBUGA
variants.text: We have fewer resident testimonies than this decision deserves.

variants.speaker: KATO
variants.text: I am not staying. But I hope this city learns what our company did not.

variants.speaker: GAIA
variants.text: Demand has fallen while essential services stayed protected.

variants.speaker: GAIA
variants.text: The grid survived. The imbalance did not.
